query: I've actually stopped reading graphic novels altogether because a few disappointing titles overshadowed my previous enjoyment of the medium. However, encountering a few titles that didn’t resonate with me at all has left a sour taste, making it hard to appreciate the genre as I once did. It’s ironic, really, because graphic novels have the potential to convey deep emotional arcs and stunning visuals, which I used to love exploring. Now, instead of excitement, I just feel hesitant whenever I browse through their pages, wondering if I'll come across another letdown instead of the captivating experience I used to cherish.
